deviations: reword.lua goes the other way from the prototype's reword.py: it turns 5.3.6's word order into LuaJIT's and is applied to PUC's output, because the .expect files must equal luajit's output exactly. It is a Lua filter, so run-bitop.sh needs no Python.

Line format is '<id> TAB <result>' with ids like '& 2^31 -1', not r3's four tab-separated fields. t_fold.expect has a third field: LuaJIT's fold decision ('folded' or 'runtime:B...'). It comes from the B reference, has no PUC counterpart, and part 2 compares only the first two fields.

Applying X per operator on PUC: t_ops wraps each op's result; t_fold rewrites each source with Lua 5.3's own precedence table (xform). In raw mode it checks the rewrite changes nothing (exit 3 otherwise). t_sar applies X to the model's result. Check (2) traces every operator's exact integer, so an inexact intermediate under an exact final result is still checked.

coerce_agree.lua is rewritten for B. 's | 0' now raises for '0x7fffffffffffffff', '9007199254740993' and '9223372036854775807' (3 false disagreements on B [M]). It now compares pack('<j') unpacked as two I4 halves against 's & 0xFFFFFFFF' and 's >> 32', both always exact. Results: B 0, b0 29, PUC 0.

Added beyond design.md: 6 string-operand extras in t_ops; 21 error-naming cases (2 of them the RESID-varinfo lines); 18 B cases in t_fold; and 2 string operands in t_sar (391 -> 437), because only a string can give ~>> an inexact result.

Added a fourth matrix script, t_bit.lua with its .expect, for the 'bit/bit32 regressions' in design.md section 6: LuaJIT's bit library on luajit.exe. bit32 is covered through the shim in bitop_test.c BT6, expected values from PUC 5.3.6's bit32. Both are regression guards that pass on b0 too, so their fail-firsts are the 64-bit bit wrapper and BT6's '1 << 32' field.
The prototype's checkhook_bit loop raises under B, so BT5 uses a loop that stays exact: s = (s ~ ((i << 28) & 0x1FFFFFFFFFFFFF)) >> 1. Expected s = 4206410837014599, from PUC 5.3.6.

'The RAM cap' in part 3 means: the C path, string operands and counts outside 0..63 included, charges the cap nothing (100000 iterations, GC stopped, the function's JIT off), next to a control that is charged. An inexact error raised at an exhausted cap is not tested: that would measure the shim's credit and window semantics, not the operators.
open_questions: Part 3 was run only against my scratch build dir (bB/src copied, lj52shim.o and eris_lj.o compiled from HEAD with -DLJ52_ADDITIVE). The main session should run it on role A's real build: OCLJ_BUILD=<scratch>/build/native sh test/native/run-bitop.sh. Before that, check the B reference's luajit.exe md5 702b747a17d5 against the shipped build's.

BT5's tick bound (> 100) comes from the build-native.sh checkhook gate. I did not build a LuaJIT without CHECKHOOK, so on its own it has no fail-first here: b0 fails BT5 only through s. The gate's own fail-first is a stock LuaJIT.

The t_fold fold column records LuaJIT's own decisions taken from the B reference. Two are not B's rule: '-0.0 | 0' runs at run time because LuaJIT's parser does not fold a negated zero, and '"3" | 4' runs at run time because it has a string. The column is not derived from PUC. Should part 2 also check it against a stated rule?
The Linux LuaJIT side is not measured [I]: no Linux B build exists. Only Linux PUC was run.

For C3 (negctl): INEXACT-SLOW is caught by every inexact line of the matrix (550 + 11 + 5) and by BT3a-d, not only by string cases, because the interpreter's fast path defers raising to the C path. t_ops barely exercises the JIT (16 traces), so JIT-side arms need C2's suites.
